cohort: Women who delivered late preterm infants between October 2019 and November 2020 (n=191)
finding: Late preterm birth was most commonly medically indicated, particularly due to maternal hypertensive disease, and was associated with increased maternal high care/ICU admissions and neonatal complications.
mod_finding: Neonates born by cesarean delivery were more likely to have respiratory complications and require NICU admission.
